items.title: Devoid of options, flood survivors return to damaged homes
items.desc: The government has announced rent assistance, temporary shelters and new land for resettlement. Survivors and local officials say little of it has reached them.

items.title: She climbed Everest without supplemental oxygen. But the summit was never the point
items.desc: Melissa Arnot Reid, the first American woman to achieve the feat, launched her memoir in Kathmandu, reflecting on shame, self-worth and the people behind Himalayan expeditions.

items.title: After years of delay, Budhigandaki faces another change of plan
items.desc: Successive governments have changed the project’s development models. Latest plan to set up an authority has raised new questions over implementation.

items.title: Oli, Dahal move to extend alliance to next year’s local and provincial polls
items.desc: UML and Nepali Communist Party leaders are exploring grassroots-level electoral cooperation to prevent further erosion of left-wing support.

items.title: Xtreme is betting on Nepali sport. It’s helping both — for now
items.desc: A Nepali energy drink is now sponsoring national cricket team players, seven NPL franchises, and the country’s first franchise volleyball league. But nobody will say how much it is paying.

items.title: Nepal, India to discuss border security at annual meeting this week
items.desc: The three-day talks will focus on cross-border crime, human trafficking, drug smuggling, boundary management and intelligence sharing along the 1,751-kilometre open border.

items.title: Choose your words carefully, minister
items.desc: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle was half right on nationalism and India. But a finance minister abroad speaks for the country, not just his party.

items.title: Nepal seeks talks with Malaysia over recruitment of Nepali workers
items.desc: Kathmandu has proposed a meeting in November or December to discuss Malaysia’s foreign worker recruitment system and renew a labour agreement signed in 2018.
